","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Prove that, the element of \( C \) is an irrational number.","marks":0,"answer":"We know \( 4 < 7 < 9 \), so \( \sqrt{4} < \sqrt{7} < \sqrt{9} \) i.e., \( 2 < \sqrt{7} < 3 \).
Thus \( \sqrt{7} \) is not an integer.
If \( \sqrt{7} \) is rational, let \( \sqrt{7} = \frac{p}{q} \), where \( p, q \) are co-prime natural numbers, \( q > 1 \).
Squaring: \( 7 = \frac{p^2}{q^2} \) ⇒ \( 7q^2 = p^2 \).
Thus \( 7 \) divides \( p^2 \), so \( 7 \) divides \( p \). Let \( p = 7k \).
Then \( 7q^2 = (7k)^2 = 49k^2 \) ⇒ \( q^2 = 7k^2 \).
Thus \( 7 \) divides \( q^2 \), so \( 7 \) divides \( q \).
But then \( p \) and \( q \) have a common factor 7, contradicting co-primality.
∴ \( \sqrt{7} \) is irrational. (Proved)
